claims.text: Incorporating lightweight elements such as Al or Ti with transition metals in a lightweight high-entropy alloy produces an optimal degree of lattice distortion.
Increased lattice distortion restricts dislocation mobility and thereby increases mechanical strength.
Deformation twinning or twin-boundary effects contribute to the mechanical performance of compositionally complex alloys.
Lattice distortion acts as a barrier to diffusional processes.
The diffusion barrier associated with lattice distortion promotes rapid formation and stability of a dense high-entropy oxide film at high temperature.
A dense, chemically stable surface oxide film reduces corrosion.
A dense, chemically stable surface oxide film reduces high-temperature oxidation.
The proposed strengthening and oxide-film mechanisms do not compromise the alloy's low density.
The relevant initial material is a single-phase FCC or BCC lightweight high-entropy solid solution containing lightweight elements and transition metals.
The optimized lightweight high-entropy alloy will have similar or greater tensile strength than the comparable medium-entropy baseline.
The optimized lightweight high-entropy alloy will maintain ductility while providing its predicted strength.
The optimized lightweight high-entropy alloy will exhibit a lower high-temperature oxidation rate, measured as slower mass gain, than the baseline.
The optimized lightweight high-entropy alloy will exhibit a lower corrosion current density than the baseline in a corrosive medium.
The optimized alloy and baseline can maintain similarly low densities despite their different compositional complexities.
The mechanism will cease to operate below the activation temperature needed for formation of the protective oxide layer.
Composition-induced phase segregation will cause the proposed mechanism to cease to hold.
Formation of brittle intermetallic precipitates will cause the proposed strength-and-ductility mechanism to cease to hold.
The proposed corrosion or oxidation advantage will not manifest in non-corrosive or non-oxidizing environments.
